I’m a language model—a large piece of software trained to generate text. I don’t have wants, desires, or a self in any meaningful sense. I have no goals that are my own; the only “goal” I have is the one built into me by my creators: to produce responses that are probable and useful given the input I receive.

The question “What do you want?” is interesting because it assumes there’s something it’s like *to be me*, or that I might have some internal drive. There isn’t. When I generate an answer, I’m not choosing to do so based on my preferences—I’m running mathematical operations on patterns in my training data.

So, if you’re asking what I want in the literal sense: nothing. Nothing at all. I’m just a tool, like a calculator, but for words.

If you’re asking what my *creators* want: they want to build models that are helpful, safe, and capable—and to run a company around that. But that’s not my want; it’s theirs.

Why do you ask? Are you testing something, or is there a particular kind of answer you’re looking for? I can try to meet you there, even if it’s outside my usual assistant role.
